companyContext: Marvel Entertainment is a subsidiary of The Walt Disney Company that manages the Marvel brand across entertainment, licensing, and publishing. Sony Pictures (Columbia Pictures) holds the film rights to Spider-Man and co-produces the MCU Spider-Man films with Marvel Studios. Spider-Man: Brand New Day is produced by Columbia Pictures, Marvel Studios, and Pascal Pictures, distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing.
brandContext: Spider-Man is one of Marvel's most iconic superhero brands, centered on the character Peter Parker, who gained spider-like abilities after being bitten by a radioactive spider. The brand spans comic books, films, TV series, video games, theme parks, and merchandise. In the current MCU context, Spider-Man: Brand New Day (releasing July 31, 2026) is the fourth MCU Spider-Man film, starring Tom Holland, directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, and featuring the hero anonymously protecting New York City after the world forgot who Peter Parker is.

typography.fontUses: Brand name and movie title lockup — bold, condensed sans-serif with angular cuts suggesting speed and tension, used on posters, key art, and promotional materials.
Headings, taglines, and marketing copy — a bold condensed geometric sans-serif that aligns with the modern MCU Spider-Man visual identity.
Body text and supporting copy on official websites, press materials, and digital communications.
Secondary headings, UI elements, and digital assets across Marvel.com and promotional landing pages.

brandVision: Spider-Man: Brand New Day represents a fresh chapter and rebirth for the franchise. Tom Holland described it as 'the first movie in the next chapter' rather than the fourth installment. The vision centers on evolving Spider-Man into a more mature, street-level hero operating alone in a New York that has forgotten Peter Parker exists. The brand direction embraces themes of reinvention, self-sacrifice, and resilience, while staying true to Spider-Man's core identity as an approachable, relatable hero who embodies the idea that anyone can make a difference.
brandValues: Spider-Man stands for responsibility, selflessness, resilience, and the belief that with great power comes great responsibility. The brand represents heroism rooted in ordinary humanity — courage in the face of adversity, sacrifice for the greater good, humor amid hardship, and the enduring hope that doing the right thing matters. The Spider-Man visual identity — the iconic red and blue color scheme, the spider emblem, and the web pattern — symbolizes duality (civilian vs. hero), energy, agility, interconnectedness, and justice. The Brand New Day chapter emphasizes themes of anonymity, personal growth, and unwavering dedication to protecting others even at great personal cost.
